about.title: Bishop Slip & Fall & Premises Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Bishop draws a steady flow of travelers along Rt 395 and US-395, along with locals shopping and dining near N Main Street and N Fowler Street. That traffic means more people moving through parking lots, motel walkways, gas station entries, and store aisles — and more chances for a wet floor, broken step, or icy patch to go unaddressed. When a property owner in Bishop knew, or reasonably should have known, about a hazard and didn't fix it or warn visitors, California law allows an injured person to pursue compensation. Because Inyo County businesses vary widely in size, evidence like surveillance footage, incident reports, and maintenance logs can disappear quickly if no one asks for it. LawProactive doesn't practice law — we simply connect you, free of charge, with an independent attorney who can evaluate what happened, gather the right records, and explain your options. There's no obligation, and no fee unless your case results in a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney About a Bishop Fall Claim

items.title: Notice Has to Be Shown
items.desc: California requires proof the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard and failed to address it. An attorney can help identify what evidence supports that timeline before it's lost.

items.title: Surveillance Video Doesn't Wait
items.desc: Many Bishop businesses along N Main Street and Rt 395 record over footage within days or weeks. An early request to preserve that video can be critical to your claim.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Reduce, Not Erase, Your Case
items.desc: Even if you're found partly responsible for the fall, California's pure comparative fault rule still allows you to recover a reduced amount rather than nothing at all.

items.question: How long do I have to file a premises liability claim in Bishop?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you two years from the date of the fall to file a lawsuit. If the property is owned by a public entity, such as a government building, the deadline is much shorter and requires an early claim filing. Talking to an attorney soon after the incident helps make sure no deadline is missed.

items.question: What should I do right after a fall at a Bishop business?
items.answer: If possible, take photos of the hazard, note the exact location, and ask an employee or manager to file an incident report. Given how much foot traffic moves through spots near N Fowler Street and US-395, requesting that surveillance footage be preserved as soon as possible can make a real difference later.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything to connect me with an attorney?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service that connects injured people with independent attorneys who work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation. We're not a law firm and don't handle your case directly.
